title: Huge Content-Length digits crash do_POST, no reply
description:
git-vouch-trqp:334-335 (Handler.do_POST). The Content-Length check calls int(length) outside any try. On Python 3.9.14+ (the floor is 3.9; tested on 3.12.3), int() of more than 4300 digits raises ValueError (CVE-2020-10735 limit), which escapes do_POST. The client gets no response at all, only a closed connection, instead of the 400 malformedRequest trust-task-error the code intends, and a full traceback goes to the log for each such request.

Reproduced (scratch copy): "POST /trust-tasks HTTP/1.0" with "Content-Length: " + "1"*5000 got an empty reply, and the log showed "ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion" from bridge.py line 335. With 4300 digits it correctly got the 400 trust-task-error.

Impact: fails closed, and only a hostile client sends this. But it breaks the "every refusal is a trust-task-error, never a traceback" contract, and gives an unauthenticated client a cheap way to fill the log (one header line up to 64 KiB, about 10 log lines per request).

Fix: reject on string length before converting, e.g. `len(length) > len(str(MAX_BODY))` alongside the isascii/isdigit test (a zero-padded but small Content-Length then gets a 400, which is fine). Test: add a 5000-digit case to test_bad_content_length_is_malformed.
close_reason: Content-Length digit count checked before int() (huge Content-Length test in test_trqp.py)
